Thanks for taking this quickly. Please see attached an initial notice from one of our partners claiming that generated outputs from one of the models you host for us reproduce portions of a third-party dataset they own. They asked us to notify you and asked for remediation and indemnification under the MSA / Order Form.

High level: the claimant points to several redacted prompts and example outputs (see p.2 of the attachment) and asserts the outputs are substantially similar to their copyrighted sample set. They're asking for:
- immediate preservation of logs and model artifacts for a 30-day period;
- a written response within 7 business days outlining technical remediation steps; and
- indemnity for any damages if the claim is substantiated.

We have an active order form (ACME-2028-REDWOOD-53) referencing the standard MSA. Our internal counsel asked that we trigger the vendor notice to you per Section 9 (Indemnification). Can you confirm Redwood's position on defense control v. customer-directed defense, and whether the Order Form contains any carveouts for training-data-derived claims?

Attaching the notice (infringement_notice.pdf). Happy to set a quick call — this is on our critical path for a partner integration.

— Sam

Kim / Laura — forwarding the notice from Acme (attached). Key asks from legal:
- Confirm whether our Order Form or MSA limits Redwood's obligations for claims arising from customer-provided prompts or downstream outputs;
- Determine whether we're willing to accept defense control or insist on contribution / indemnity from Acme for claims tied to their inputs; and
- Identify required evidence preservation steps (logs, KV cache snapshots, training data provenance).

My read: our standard MSA limits third-party IP indemnity to infringement caused by the model itself (i.e., model weights / training input that we control) but the Order Form has a blank on the "customer content" carveout. For Sales's part, Acme negotiated a narrower indemnity from us to keep purchase moving. I'm attaching a draft with inline notes (redlines_suggested.docx) — mostly targeted at keeping defense control but accepting a limited contribution structure if Acme can show the claim relates to their prompts or a customer dataset.

Can you review and propose an external response that:
1) Asks for evidence of copying (specific examples and similarity metric);
2) Preserves logs and requests chain-of-custody;
3) If we move to defend, makes defense control a must with right to approve settlement;
4) Suggests insurance/limits as an alternative (carrier contact, policy language).

If we can't square this quickly, I'd like to escalate to Sales leadership for potential concessions (credits, repair timeline) — but that's last resort.

— Rishi

Sam —

Thanks for flagging and for sending the notice. We've reviewed the claimant's examples and the initial notice you provided. We'd like to propose the following interim position while we collect more evidence: 

1) Evidence & Preservation: Redwood will preserve relevant logs, request histories, and model invocation metadata for a 90-day window. We'll need Acme's help to identify the specific prompt sets and timestamps you relied on so we can pull matching traces.

2) Scope of Indemnity & Defense Control: Our standard MSA limits indemnity for third-party IP to claims arising from the model weights and training corpus we control. We are willing to defend and indemnify only to the extent the claimant can link the infringement to model training artifacts under Redwood's control. Where claims arise from customer-provided inputs or downstream transformations (including prompts or datasets Acme supplied), we will request contribution from Acme.

3) Proposed Compromise (to avoid immediate escalation): Redwood will:
- Lead the defense (defense control) for covered claims, with the right to select counsel and to approve settlements;
- Accept a capped indemnity exposure tied to the Order Form limit (proposed: $1.5M), subject to proof of copying of training material;
- Require prompt notice and cooperation per Section 9.3.

4) Insurance & Remedies: If Acme would prefer not to have Redwood's defense control, we can agree to a negotiated contribution model and ask Acme to direct its carrier to coordinate coverage. I've attached a short memorandum with suggested language (proposed_responses.docx) and our insurance summary (insurance_summary.pdf).

Next steps: can you provide the specific prompt examples and any contract references in your order form that you believe change our standard allocation? We'd like to avoid a hardline "you defend / you pay" fight if possible — happy to take a call tomorrow to align.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
